piece.title: String Quartet in C major, Hob.III:77, Op.76 No.3 (“Emperor”)
piece.movement: II. Poco adagio; cantabile — Var. II
piece.why: Variation II: the hymn moves to the cello while Violin I plays a busy countermelody above it. Both planners mislabel the violin as the tune here; the cello's hymn is still kept.

roster.label: Church brass: 2 trumpets (one beginner), horn, euphonium

plan.summary: As written (no arranging): the original parts are handed out unchanged. The source parts in score order (Violin 1, Violin 2, Viola and Violoncello) are paired with the players sorted from highest to lowest range center (the midpoint of each player's sounding range): Violin 1 → Trumpet 1; Violin 2 → Trumpet 2 (beginner); Viola → Horn in F; Violoncello → Euphonium. No octave shifts, no chord changes beyond what a one-note instrument requires (a wind or brass player plays the top note of a double stop or chord), and no repair: a note outside a player's range stays where it is and is marked with an x notehead.

assignments.reason: as written: Violin 1 goes to Trumpet 1, the highest range center (sounding F3–F5); no octave shift, no repair
as written: Violin 2 goes to Trumpet 2 (beginner), the 2nd highest range center (sounding A♭3–B♭4); no octave shift, no repair
as written: Viola goes to Horn in F, the 3rd highest range center (sounding C3–C5); no octave shift, no repair
as written: Violoncello goes to Euphonium, the 4th highest range center (sounding F2–F4); no octave shift, no repair
